name: Cosmos
grown_as: A half-hardy annual raised under cover and planted out after frost. William's library lists 'Fizzy Rose Picotee': semi-double flowers, mainly white, the petals edged and stained dark pinkish-red, about 0.9 m. Drawn as that. ⚠️ CHECK
habit: A tall, airy, branched annual 0.6 to 1.2 m high, the stems thin, smooth and often reddish, the whole plant light and feathery.

leaf.type: Compound: twice divided (bipinnate) into many very fine, thread-like segments, like a feather or fennel
leaf.outline: The whole leaf broadly oval to triangular, 10 to 20 cm long; each segment 1 mm wide and 1 to 4 cm long
leaf.base: The leaf sits almost straight on the stem
leaf.tip: Each segment ends in a fine point
leaf.veins: Only a midrib in each segment

flower.form: An open, flat to shallow-bowled daisy. 'Fizzy' types are semi-double: a ring of broad outer rays with a frilly tuft of extra short rays round the centre
flower.petals: Eight broad outer rays (in a single flower), wedge-shaped, overlapping a little, the broad tip with three or more small uneven teeth and fine parallel lines along each ray
flower.colour: Mainly white, edged and streaked dark pinkish-red (picotee). The species is pink, magenta or white
flower.centre: A small yellow disc of tubular florets, slightly domed; partly hidden by the frill in semi-double flowers
flower.behind: Two rows of bracts: the outer narrow, pointed and green, spreading; the inner broad, thin and pale with brown lines, pressed to the head
flower.carried: Alone on long, thin, bare stalks held high above the leaves, facing up or outwards

fruit: A loose starburst of long, narrow seeds pointing outwards from the top of the stalk, each dark brown to black, about 1 cm, with two or three short barbed bristles at the tip.
seedling: Two long, narrow, strap-shaped seed leaves. The first true leaves are already cut into narrow lobes, feathery from the start.
winter: Nothing: killed by the first frost.

leaf: leaf cut twice into thread-like segments, feathery
bloom: broad wedge-shaped rays with small teeth at the tips
a frill of short extra rays round a small yellow centre (semi-double)
seed: two or three short bristles at the top
seedling: first true leaves already divided and feathery
young: upright branching plant with fine feathery foliage
flower: flowers held singly on long bare stalks well above the feathery foliage
seedhead: a starburst of narrow dark seeds pointing outwards from the stalk tip

look_alikes: Cosmos sulphureus is orange or yellow with broader leaf segments. Single dahlias have broad leaflets. Coreopsis is yellow with narrow but flatter leaf lobes. Mayweeds have thread-like leaves but small white daisies with large yellow centres.
